card.name: Commas and linkers in side-effect lists
card.fires_on: Commas, 'and', 'and/or' or 'additive' that come right after a first listed effect in drug-interaction text, mainly anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, constipation) and heart effects (inotropic, chronotropic, conduction).

modes.label: Comma after dry mouth
modes.description: The comma after dry mouth or xerostomia in a list of anticholinergic side effects.
modes.example: may increase the frequency and/or severity of dry mouth<<,>> constipation, blurred vision, and other

modes.label: Linker in heart-effect pairs
modes.description: 'and' or 'and/or' joining paired cardiac effects such as inotropic and chronotropic or contractility and conduction.
modes.example: Disopyramide is a Type I antiarrhythmic drug with potent negative inotropic<< and>> chronotropic effects.

modes.label: Additive effects
modes.description: The word 'additive' or 'decrease' introducing a combined effect when two drugs are given together.
modes.example: Anticholinergic drugs administered concurrently with PA may produce<< additive>> antivagal effects on A-V nod

card.plain: It fires on the small joining words and commas that lead into the next effect in a list of drug-interaction effects.
